earlier_scan.source_named: Obersteiner, Katrin. 2019. Nominal classification in Kairak - A comparison with Mali, Qaqet and Ura. MA thesis, Universitat zu Koln.
earlier_scan.note: Only descriptive work on Kairak; a thesis of this kind plausibly includes a phonology sketch with stress; no online copy found.

sources.note: Catalog only: lists PARADISEC MS2-005 and MS2-NotesQairak (Meinrad Scheller tapes and notes, 1966), Glottolog, Ethnologue, LINGUIST List and two PARADISEC music/video items; no language description of Kairak is registered.

sources.note: Bibliographic only; no phonology or grammar entry exists for Kairak; hh.bib records the alternative spelling 'Qairaq'.

sources.citation: Stebbins, Tonya N. 2011. Mali (Baining) grammar (Pacific Linguistics 623). Canberra: ANU. (already held by the project)
sources.note: Describes Mali, not Kairak. On Kairak it says only (p.2) that 'A reference to a Kairak grammar and dictionary (Mayerhofer 1940, listed in Carrington 1996:259) seems to refer to a lost work' and that very limited material exists for Baining languages other than Mali and Kaket; no Kairak stress statement.

sources.citation: Stebbins, Tonya N. 2009. The Papuan languages of the Eastern Bismarcks: migration, origins and connections. In Bethwyn Evans (ed.), Discovering history through language: papers in honour of Malcolm Ross (Pacific Linguistics 605), 223-243. Canberra: ANU. (whole volume PDF from ANU Open Research, hdl 1885/146753, CC BY-SA 4.0)
sources.note: Nothing. Kairak appears only in classification tables and the research-history paragraph (p.227: 'A description of Kairak is currently being developed by Cindy Schneider at the University of New England'); the chapter contains no Kairak phonology and no stress/accent statement for any Baining language.

sources.citation: Schneider, Cindy (University of New England). Unpublished Kairak/Qairaq description and field materials (announced in Stebbins 2009:227 as 'currently being developed'); cf. Schneider 2011 AJL 31:187-209 (doi:10.1080/07268602.2011.560828), 2015 CILP 16:335-354, 2016 WLL 19(1) for context.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists at the publisher (DOI recorded); open or paywalled, not checked
sources.note: Schneider did sustained fieldwork in the Qairaq community; any sketch grammar or phonology she drafted would be the first-hand source for stress. The published papers are applied/sociolinguistic but may contain a short language profile.

sources.citation: Hellwig, Birgit. 2019. A grammar of Qaqet (Mouton Grammar Library 79). Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. Ch.1-2 (Baining family overview, phonology).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Closest fully described sister language from the same Cologne group that produced Obersteiner 2019; introduction compares the Baining languages and may comment on Kairak prosody.

sources.citation: Obersteiner, Katrin. 2019. Nominal classification in Kairak -- A comparison with Mali, Qaqet and Ura. MA thesis, Institut für Linguistik, Universität zu Köln (supervisor circle of B. Hellwig).

sources.note: The only modern descriptive work devoted to Kairak; an MA thesis built on the author's own field data very likely opens with a phonology/orthography sketch that would state stress. Obtain from the author or the Cologne institute.

sources.citation: Stebbins, Tonya, Bethwyn Evans & Angela Terrill. 2018. The Papuan languages of Island Melanesia. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area, 775-894. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
